pages.text: "I won't sleep! More pinecones to stack!" Nils the little bear built a pinecone tower by the stove. It was dark outside. Hoot, hoot went an owl. Nils held back a yawn. "A little more!"
Grandpa Bruno came with a lamp. "Owl calls mean bedtime." "No, not sleepy! I'll stack it to the roof!" Nils shook his head and hugged the tower.
Yaaawn! His mouth opened wide, and his eyes narrowed to threads. A pinecone slipped beneath his loosened paw. "Oh? Maybe I'm a little sleepy...?" Nils wrinkled his nose.
Grandpa sat Nils on his lap. "Look, the stove fire seems sleepy too." The big flames had become small and flickering. "A smaller fire means the cabin is getting ready for sleep. Let's join in."
First, put the stove fire to bed! Grandpa gently covered it with ash. The flames shrank. Nils repeated, "Sleep tight, fire." Only one lamp remained.
Second, under the covers! In the loft, Nils pulled them over him. Grandpa bent and rubbed his nose against Nils's forehead. He sang softly, "Owl says hoot—sleep tight!"
Third, blow out the lamp! The loft was dark, but not scary: starlight came through the window. Hoot, hoot, the owl called again. Under the covers, Nils whispered along, "Owl says hoot—sleep tight!"
Now Nils's turn. He sang softly to the owl outside. "Owl, sleep tight too. Good night." Grandpa's broad palm gently patted the covers.
Now Nils knew the bedtime order. "One, owl hoots, stop playing! Two, put the stove fire to bed! Three, under the covers, blow out the lamp!" The blanket rose and fell with his breaths.

Tap, tap, tap! Nils opened his eyes and lifted both paws high. "One lamp last night, but now the window is bright, right?" Grandpa lifted him. Sleep when the owl calls, and you can use the whole morning. Nils smiled. "Owl says hoot—sleep tight!"
